description:
Phase 6 parallel task under epic `026fc832`. 98336ab4's n=4096 measurements (commit `3dca7bf7`) reveal that Route A (GF(251)) and fp_medium (GF(65521)) reach ~36-43% of f32 FMA peak throughput on Zen 3, while fflas-ffpack's single-thread reference (verified single-thread per `dev/bench_results/2026-05-24-a70b1c70-phase0-controls.md:24`) reaches ~70%. The user-approved decision (session 6, 2026-05-25) is to close the gap in pure Rust + AVX2 — no BLAS dependency.

## Amendment (2026-05-26, user-approved, session 8)

**SC#2 (GF(65521) at n=4096) is amended to defer the remaining +17% gap to follow-up task `695350fd`** ("fp_medium u16-lane BLIS MC/KC restructure (74ba1cdc Phase 6b)"). User approval was given via the session-8 escalation after R1 closed GF(251)/4096 PASS (ratio 1.466) but left GF(65521)/4096 SHORTFALL (ratio 1.753). The R1 worker's MR=3 and MR=4 fp_medium register-tile attempts both regressed (-21% and -35%) due to register spills; closing GF(65521) cleanly needs the BLIS-style MC/KC restructure scoped in `695350fd`.

**Amended SC#2 reads:** "GF(65521) at n=4096 PASS via follow-up `695350fd`. Within 74ba1cdc, the partial improvement is documented (39.78 Gop/s vs 36.34 baseline = +9.5%, ratio 1.92 → 1.753); full closure is the responsibility of `695350fd`."

**Amended SC#8 reads:** "98336ab4's full-PASS re-bench depends on `695350fd` landing (not `74ba1cdc` alone). DAG re-wired: `98336ab4` now depends on `695350fd` instead of `74ba1cdc`."

Original SC#2 + SC#8 preserved in the **Original Success Criteria** subsection below for audit. All other SCs (#1, #3-#7) remain `[hard]` and are verified for 74ba1cdc closure.

## Background

Measured at n=4096 (5-trial CCX1-pinned, post-`3dca7bf7`):

| Prime | gf2 Gop/s | gf2 GFLOPS | fflas Gop/s | fflas GFLOPS | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GF(251) | 85.22 | ~43 | 158.96 | ~80 | 1.87× |
| GF(65521) | 36.34 | ~18 | 69.72 | ~35 | 1.92× |

Theoretical Zen 3 f32 FMA peak: ~118 GFLOPS/core. OpenBLAS sgemm runs at ~70% of peak; Route A at ~36%.

Closing the gap to PASS (ratio ≤ 1.5×, i.e. ≥ 0.667) requires ~25% per-core throughput improvement on Route A and fp_medium.

## Scope

Engineer Route A and fp_medium with better cache + register-tile + accumulation discipline. Concrete levers (impl agent picks the productive subset):

1. **BLIS-style 3-level cache blocking.** Add MC (rows) + NC (cols) cache blocking levels above the existing KC = 256. Repack the A panel into a contiguous packed buffer (`PackedF32Panel<MC, KC>`) reused across multiple NC chunks of B. Persistent packed-A cache across `gemm` calls of the same shape.
2. **Deeper register tiling.** Current 4×24 tile uses ~12 of 16 AVX2 registers. Sweep MR × NR variants: 6×16, 8×12, 4×32 (limited by f32 lane count). Pick the variant that minimises spills on Zen 3.
3. **Longer Barrett-reduction window.** Route A currently reduces every k = 512. Compute the maximum k that avoids f32 mantissa overflow given $p \le 251$ and lane count; extend the window. fp_medium similarly: extend the u16-pack reduction window.
4. **Persistent panel packing.** When the same A matrix is reused across multiple `gemm` calls (e.g., in PLE recursion), cache the packed-A representation. This pays off in `fp_small_panel.rs`'s current strategy but is currently per-call.
5. **Prefetching.** Add `_mm_prefetch` hints for the B-panel ahead of the inner loop. Tune the lookahead distance.

## Success Criteria (current — amended 2026-05-26)

- [hard] GF(251) at n=4096: ratio gf2/fflas ≤ 1.5× (gf2 wall ≤ 1.5× fflas wall) on 5-trial CCX1-pinned bench on the Zen 3 reference host.
- [hard] [AMENDED 2026-05-26 — see Amendment block above] GF(65521) at n=4096 PASS via follow-up `695350fd`. Within 74ba1cdc, document the partial improvement (39.78 Gop/s vs 36.34 baseline = +9.5%, ratio 1.92 → 1.753) in the evidence doc; full closure deferred to `695350fd`.
- [hard] No regression on existing PASS cells at n ∈ {64, 256, 1024} for GF(7), GF(31), GF(127), GF(241), GF(251), GF(65521) (delta ≤ 5% on CCX1-pinned bench with warmup-matched protocol; use the same 5-trial setup as `dev/bench_results/2026-05-25-41096af5-post-wire-in-aggregate.csv`).
- [hard] Bit-exact correctness preserved (proptest sweep at boundary lengths {0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65} for all 6 primes).
- [hard] No BLAS dependency. No external linker change. Pure Rust + AVX2.
- [hard] Unsafe stays in `gf2-kernels-simd` (no new unsafe in `gf2-core`).
- [hard] Evidence doc at `dev/bench_results/2026-05-<date>-<this-id>-fgemm-engineering.md` records before/after numbers, the techniques applied, and a non-regression sweep across all (prime, n) cells.
- [hard] [AMENDED 2026-05-26 — see Amendment block above] 98336ab4's full-PASS re-bench depends on `695350fd` landing (not `74ba1cdc` alone). DAG re-wired: `98336ab4` now depends on `695350fd` instead of `74ba1cdc`.

## Original Success Criteria (pre-amendment, preserved for audit)

- [hard] GF(65521) at n=4096: ratio gf2/fflas ≤ 1.5× on 5-trial CCX1-pinned bench.
- [hard] After this task lands, 98336ab4 worker re-benches all n=4096 cells with warmup-matched protocol; 98336ab4 closes PASS for all 6 cells (including the GF(7)/256 -37.3% delta from instruction-cache warmup, which is fixable as part of this task's bench re-run).

## Out of scope

- AVX-512 (epic `7f809931`).
- BLAS delegation (explicitly excluded per user directive).
- Multi-threading the single-matrix `gemm` (separate epic if pursued).

## Notes

- Filed session 6 (2026-05-25) after wave-6 review + user decision.
- R0 dispatch hit a wall (host contention + architectural depth); evidence doc `dev/bench_results/2026-05-25-74ba1cdc-fgemm-engineering.md` recommended Phase 6a/6b decomposition.
- R1 dispatch (serial, flock-guarded, post-session-6 user choice "Option B") landed Route A PASS + fp_medium partial improvement. Evidence doc `dev/bench_results/2026-05-26-74ba1cdc-fgemm-engineering.md` documents the R1 work.
- Phase 6b follow-up `695350fd` was filed session 8 (2026-05-26) per user-approved deferral of SC#2.
- Independent of the panelized-PLE / echelon / invert / solve track.
- Reference: BLIS paper (Van Zee & van de Geijn 2015, "BLIS: A Framework for Rapidly Instantiating BLAS Functionality"), Goto-Geijn 2008 algorithm.
title: Improve single-thread fgemm engineering: Route A + fp_medium at n=4096
